title: What If the World's Population Started Shrinking?

scenes.text: What if the world's population started shrinking? Dozens of countries are already past their peak.
The UN counts 63 countries and areas whose populations peaked before 2024, home to 28 percent of humanity.
Worldwide, women now average 2.3 births, down from 3.3 in 1990. More than half of countries are below the 2.1 needed to stay stable.
The UN expects the world to peak at about 10.3 billion people in the mid-2080s.
Then a slow decline, to about 10.2 billion by 2100.
The bigger shift is age. By the 2070s, people over 65 will outnumber children under 18.
